thirtySeconds: KeithK75 owned Shinnecock Hills, taking the net title at +1 by eight shots over HamSammich and completing the sweep with the gross win at -3. The raw-golf gap was enormous: Keith gained 17.79 total strokes, including 8.05 on approach and 6.68 around the green, while HamSammich survived on putting and net help despite losing strokes tee to green. Dan94 was the gross runner-up at +19 with 6.79 total strokes gained, but the net board belonged to Keith from the opening bell.
latestTournamentTeaser: KeithK75 demolished the net race at Shinnecock Hills, winning by eight shots while also posting the only gross score under par at -3. Dan94 had the second-best gross score, but Keith’s 17.79 strokes gained made this one tough to argue with.

carnage.name: Dan94
carnage.commentary: The opening drive found deeprough, then the recovery found fairway, then another recovery found fairway, and the next four shots somehow still left him 20 yards from the hole. He finally reached the green from 27 yards, missed the 19-footer by a foot, and tapped in for the nine-stroke crime scene.

carnage.name: IUDoc92
carnage.commentary: A drive into deeprough turned into a sand visit, followed by three straight attempts to locate the fairway from progressively less useful distances. From 30 yards he left 26 feet, burned a 25-footer, and cleaned up for eight.

carnage.name: DREADFUL
carnage.commentary: The first ball went to deeprough, the next one to fairway, then the next two wandered between fairway and deeprough like they were avoiding responsibility. He eventually reached the green from 19 yards, missed an 11-footer by an inch, and signed for seven on a par three.

carnage.name: Leroy4522
carnage.commentary: The tee shot went to deeprough, the second shot reached fairway, and the third reached fairway again, which sounds encouraging until you notice he was still 23 yards out. A 32-footer became a 9-footer, then an 11-footer, then a 3-footer. Eight shots, one green, zero momentum.

carnage.name: HamSammich
carnage.commentary: Three consecutive shots into deeprough turned a 234-yard hole into a 46-yard rescue mission. He finally found fairway, crept to the green, and tapped in from six feet for a seven that somehow still counted as a net six.

carnage.name: KeithK75
carnage.commentary: A perfectly serviceable drive and approach were followed by a 165-yard expedition into deeprough. The shot log then skips number four, because even the data seems embarrassed, before Keith pitches to 19 yards, gets to 11 feet, and holes the putt for seven.

carnage.name: MashedBROtato
carnage.commentary: The tee shot missed into rough, the second shot found fairway, and the third finally reached green from 21 yards. He left the 19-footer two feet short and tapped in for five, a modest disaster by the standards of this leaderboard.

players.name: KeithK75
players.tagline: Approach play so good it made Shinnecock look negotiable.
players.body: KeithK75 won the net competition at +1 and the gross competition at -3, finishing eight shots clear of HamSammich. The score was backed by the round’s best raw golf: 17.79 total strokes gained, with 8.05 on approach, 6.68 in the short game, and 2.44 putting. He hit 10 greens, made four birdies, avoided every bogey and double bogey, and needed only 24 putts. His worst hole was still a seven, but after the deeprough detour he holed the 11-footer to stop the bleeding. Across seven prior starts, Keith already owned four gross wins and averaged a 1.57 gross finish; this was another loud confirmation that the ball-striking is not a fluke.

players.name: HamSammich
players.tagline: The putter kept bailing out a tee-to-green hostage situation.
players.body: HamSammich took the net runner-up spot at +9 despite a gross +37, eight shots behind Keith and 18 behind Dan94’s gross score. The useful part was the putting, worth 2.37 strokes gained, plus a modest 0.66 off the tee. Everywhere else was a fight: approach was -2.06, tee to green was -1.58, and four greens in regulation turned the round into repeated short-game paperwork. His seven on the par-four featured three straight balls into deeprough before a six-foot finish, while his card also included seven bogeys and four doubles. That matches the five-start profile: strong net finishes can happen, but the underlying golf has averaged -2.16 total strokes gained and -2.98 tee to green.

players.name: MashedBROtato
players.tagline: Big drives, small fairway count, medium-sized survival skills.
players.body: MashedBROtato posted +15 net and +39 gross, with 4.79 total strokes gained keeping the round from becoming a full coastal evacuation. Approach led the good work at 3.07, supported by 0.92 in the short game, while putting was essentially neutral at 0.02. The 317-yard longest drive and 305 average on fairways supplied plenty of distance, but only three fairways and six greens in regulation left too much cleanup, producing eight bogeys and two doubles. He did flash quality with a net eagle on the par four where he holed a 25-footer, but the worst hole was a five on a par three after needing three shots to get from rough to green. After seven prior starts with a -0.12 average total strokes gained, this was a meaningful step forward in the raw numbers even if the net result stayed ordinary.

players.name: Dan94
players.tagline: A polished ball-striking round ruined by one very long afternoon.
players.body: Dan94 was the gross runner-up at +19 with 6.79 total strokes gained, including 3.63 approach and 5.71 tee to green, but his +27 net score left him fourth in the actual league race. The card had eight fairways, seven greens, zero doubles, and only 31 putts, so the baseline golf was solid. Then came the par-five nine: a deeprough drive, two recovery shots that still left him 19 yards out, three more short-game attempts, and a 19-footer that stopped one foot short. That nine did the damage. His seven-start profile remains built on excellent gross play—1.71 average gross finish and 12.04 average total strokes gained—but the net conversion still has not produced a win.

players.name: DREADFUL
players.tagline: Every department filed a complaint, especially the putter.
players.body: DREADFUL finished at +27 net and +75 gross, with -12.21 total strokes gained and no positive category to hide behind. The tee was the main wreck at -6.09, putting added -4.34, and just three greens in regulation forced a steady diet of damage control. The par-three seven was the cleanest summary: deeprough, fairway, fairway, deeprough, then a 12-footer that missed by an inch. He made no birdies, carded eight doubles, and needed 35 putts with three three-putts. Over seven prior starts, the profile was already negative at -6.42 total strokes gained per appearance; this round confirmed the issue rather than challenging it.

players.name: IUDoc92
players.tagline: One holed-out par five could not rescue the rest of the map.
players.body: IUDoc92 posted +32 net and +72 gross, finishing with -10.21 total strokes gained. The round had only two greens in regulation, six bogeys, six doubles, and 34 putts, with tee play at -3.49 and short game at -3.90. The par-four disaster was impressively thorough: deeprough off the tee, sand on the second, then three attempts from around the fairway before finally reaching the green and two-putting from 26 feet. He did hole out from 18 yards for a net eagle on the par five, and made a nine-footer for birdie later, but those flashes could not offset the larger pattern. His seven-start history sits at -9.34 total strokes gained per appearance, so this was harshly familiar territory.

players.name: Leroy4522
players.tagline: The golf ball spent the day sightseeing outside the fairways.
players.body: Leroy4522 finished at +28 net and +55 gross with -11.21 total strokes gained. He found just one green in regulation, hit four fairways, made no birdies, and needed 36 putts with four three-putts. The short game was -4.05, approach was -2.04, and tee play was -3.55, a complete loss of ground from tee to green. His worst hole became an eight after the opening deeprough miss, three recovery shots, a 32-footer, a 41-footer, a 20-footer, and finally a three-footer. There were a few quality finishes later in the round, including a net birdie on the par four, but seven prior starts already showed a -5.84 average total strokes gained and a 6.86 average net finish. The profile stayed stubbornly on brand.

stateOfLeague: KeithK75 strengthened an already dominant profile: after seven prior starts with two net wins, four gross wins, and a 1.57 average gross finish, he now owns both sides of the Shinnecock result. Dan94’s gross game remains dangerous but still has no net win, while HamSammich’s net result again outran a negative tee-to-green profile. The broader league split is getting clearer: raw-golf strength and net success are not always arriving in the same package.
